articles.title: Dubai Gold Slips Below Dh500 as Shoppers Bring Forward Festive Jewellery Buying
articles.excerpt: 24-karat gold fell to Dh497.25 a gram in Dubai, its second day under the Dh500 mark, as UAE shoppers lock in purchases ahead of Navratri, Dhanteras and Diwali.
articles.image_caption: Gold necklaces and jewellery displayed in a Dubai showroom window. 24-karat gold slipped below Dh500 a gram in Dubai, with shoppers bringing forward festive purchases ahead of Navratri, Dhanteras and Diwali.
articles.nri_angle: Dubai's gold market is central to the Indian diaspora's festive shopping; sub-Dh500 rates plus rate-lock offers give UAE-based NRIs and India-bound visitors a concrete buying window ahead of Navratri, Dhanteras and Diwali.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India Express Adds Direct Riyadh, Bahrain Flights From Thiruvananthapuram
articles.excerpt: Air India Express will launch thrice-weekly Thiruvananthapuram–Riyadh and twice-weekly Thiruvananthapuram–Bahrain services on October 27, 2026, with bookings already open.
articles.image_caption: An Air India Express aircraft — the airline adds direct Thiruvananthapuram–Riyadh and Thiruvananthapuram–Bahrain flights from October 27
articles.nri_angle: Direct Riyadh and Bahrain flights cut the transfer burden for the large Kerala diaspora working in the Gulf, for whom Thiruvananthapuram is the home airport.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Bets on a 'Digital Tourism Stack' to Unify Its Fragmented Travel Market
articles.excerpt: The Ministry of Tourism and ONDC have launched the National Digital Tourism Stack, an open, AI-first infrastructure meant to make 23,000 homestays and experiences discoverable and bookable across platforms by 2028.
articles.image_caption: A graphic depicts the ONDC National Digital Tourism Stack alongside Indian landmarks including a fort, temples, the Taj Mahal, and a houseboat. The initiative aims to unify India’s fragmented travel booking market on an open digital platform.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs booking home-region homestays, guides, and experiences face India's booking fragmentation most acutely; a single verified stack with unified payments in their preferred language would collapse that planning work — and second-generation visitors without family networks gain the most.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amazon Now Takes Ultra-Fast Delivery to 120+ Indian Cities Ahead of Festive Season
articles.excerpt: The e-commerce giant doubled Amazon Now's footprint in two weeks to more than 120 cities with nearly 800 fulfilment centres, timed just before the Great Indian Festival that begins October 8.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs sending Diwali gifts and groceries to family back home can now order on Amazon Now for relatives in 120+ cities — and the Great Indian Festival from October 8 offers the season's best deals, with 10% SBI discounts and extra Prime savings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India Launches Great Escape Sale With International Fares From $350
articles.excerpt: Bookings close October 3 for the limited-period sale, which covers Air India and Air India Express flights to 40-plus destinations with travel valid through March 2027 for North American travelers.
articles.nri_angle: The sale is tailor-made for NRIs in the US and Canada planning festive-season and year-end visits to India, when demand and fares typically surge, and its coverage of routes beyond India makes stopovers in the Gulf or Southeast Asia easy to add.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Inside The Oven Diner: a Kolkata café styled like a 250-year-old rajbari
articles.excerpt: At Rajkutir in Kankurgachi, pillared halls, a vintage carriage and glowing lamps recreate a Bengali zamindar mansion — and the food, per bloggers, lives up to the setting.
articles.image_caption: The Oven Diner, inside Raajkutir in Kankurgachi, recreates the grandeur of a Bengali rajbari — pillared halls, a vintage horse-drawn carriage and glowing lamps.
articles.nri_angle: Bengali diaspora visitors get a rooted, photogenic dining stop for Kolkata trips, especially around Durga Puja season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Banswara: inside Rajasthan's 'City of 100 Islands' and its tribal heritage
articles.excerpt: About 150 km south of Udaipur, the Mahi River braids into hundreds of islets around a district rich in Bhil history, Shakti Peetha temples and monsoon waterfalls.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs with Rajasthani roots, Banswara offers uncrowded tribal heritage and freedom-struggle history at Mangarh Dham beyond the usual Jaipur-Udaipur circuit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Philippine Airlines Returns to India With Nonstop Manila-Delhi and Mumbai Flights
articles.excerpt: The Philippine flag carrier will fly nonstop from Manila to Delhi three times a week and Mumbai four times weekly from December 2026, pending Indian government approval — eight years after an earlier plan never took off.
articles.nri_angle: Direct Manila flights give the Philippines' Indian community its first nonstop link to India, cut journey times for diaspora travellers to Boracay and Cebu, and add a future oneworld option for Australia and North America routings via Manila.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Qantas Sets Mid-2028 for First Nonstop Sydney–New York Flights
articles.excerpt: The 18-hour Project Sunrise service, on sale from August 2027, will be the first commercial nonstop link between Australia and New York.
articles.image_caption: A Qantas Airbus A350-1000ULR in rendering over the New York skyline. Qantas will fly the ultra-long-range jet nonstop between Sydney and New York from mid-2028.
articles.nri_angle: Faster Australia–US links serve the large Indian-Australian community and add capacity on a corridor heavily used by diaspora travelers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Diwali 2026: India's Best Places to Experience the Festival of Lights
articles.excerpt: From a million diyas on Varanasi's ghats to the Golden Temple mirrored in light, here is where Diwali 2026 will be most spectacular — plus when to book before fares spike.
articles.image_caption: Diyas float on the Ganges during Dev Deepawali in Varanasi — the "Diwali of the gods" held two weeks after Diwali. Diwali 2026 falls in early November.
articles.nri_angle: Written for diaspora families planning a Diwali trip home — when to book from the US, where the festival is most spectacular, and how regional traditions differ.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Warns Against Using Visa-Free Malaysia Entry to Find Jobs
articles.excerpt: India's High Commission in Kuala Lumpur says it has seen a "noticeable increase" in travellers misusing the 30-day visa-free facility to seek work, warning of overstay, exploitation, detention and legal action.
articles.image_caption: A busy daytime street in Kuala Lumpur's Bukit Bintang district, with billboards and the elevated monorail line. India has warned travellers against using Malaysia's visa-free entry to seek work.
articles.nri_angle: Malaysia is home to one of the largest Indian-origin populations in Southeast Asia, and many job-seekers from India are drawn there — the advisory warns that legal employment requires a work permit or VDR, not a tourist entry.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nayanthara's ₹8 Lakh Maldives Weekend Shows the Cost of a Water Villa
articles.excerpt: The actor's holiday photos from Patina Maldives put a number on the island's top-tier luxury — a two-night stay in a Sunset Water Pool Villa runs close to ₹8 lakh, while the resort's entry-level villas cost about a third of that.
articles.image_caption: Nayanthara in a yellow dress on a Maldives beach. Her two-night water-villa getaway cost roughly ₹8 lakh, according to the report.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian travelers, Nayanthara's Maldives trip is a reminder that the island's famous prices span a wide band — celebrity-tier water villas run close to ₹4 lakh a night while beach pool villas at the same resort cost about a third of that.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Diwali Airfare Surge: Delhi–Bengaluru Tickets Cross ₹20,000 as Festival Rush Squeezes Seats
articles.excerpt: A viral post spotlighting a ₹13,000-to-₹20,000+ jump on the Delhi–Bengaluru route has become the face of this year's festive fare surge, as tighter seat capacity, costlier jet fuel and dynamic pricing collide ahead of the November 8 festival.
articles.image_caption: An Air India aircraft in flight during peak festive-season travel. Delhi-Bengaluru fares for Diwali have surged past Rs 20,000, up from around Rs 13,000, prompting complaints from travellers about festive pricing.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs combining international trips with domestic legs — or booking family members' festive-season travel within India — face the same Diwali fare surge, making early booking of domestic connections the simplest hedge.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Etihad Cancels Delhi-Abu Dhabi Flight EY217, Stranding 200 After Mid-Boarding Snag
articles.excerpt: Passengers had already boarded the Boeing 787-9 on Saturday night when the crew reported a technical issue; the cancellation was confirmed only after hours of waiting, disrupting onward connections through Etihad's Abu Dhabi hub.
articles.image_caption: An Etihad aircraft. The airline cancelled Delhi-Abu Dhabi flight EY217 mid-boarding, stranding around 200 passengers.
articles.nri_angle: Abu Dhabi is a key transit hub for US–India diaspora travellers, and a cancelled late-night feeder flight like EY217 unspools onward itineraries to Europe and North America — making clear airline communication, not just rebooking, the real test for visa-constrained travellers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India Takes Best Airline and Best Staff Titles at 2026 Skytrax Awards
articles.excerpt: The carrier beat IndiGo to the top of the India & South Asia ranking in the passenger-voted awards, adding a 4-Star certification and Most Improved Airline in Asia to a haul announced in London on September 18.
articles.image_caption: An Air India aircraft. The airline won Best Airline and Best Staff titles at the 2026 Skytrax Awards.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American travellers on Air India's large India–US nonstop network now have passenger-voted evidence — 24.8 million survey responses — that the carrier's service turnaround is real, ahead of peak Diwali and holiday-season bookings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vande Bharat Drone Video Captures Jharkhand's Hills Looking Like Switzerland
articles.excerpt: A viral aerial clip shows the saffron-and-grey Vande Bharat Express threading through dense forests and rolling hills on the Barkakana–Ranchi line, prompting viewers to compare India's heartland with the Swiss Alps.
articles.image_caption: A Vande Bharat Express train photographed near Mumbai. The viral drone video that sparked comparisons with Switzerland was filmed on the Barkakana–Ranchi line in Jharkhand.
articles.nri_angle: Jharkhandi and Bihari diaspora communities abroad get a reframed visual identity of home, with the viral clip circulating in community groups and shaping trip planning.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seven places Bollywood stars keep returning to that aren't Goa or Maldives
articles.excerpt: Beyond Goa and the Maldives, Bollywood's most loyal holiday rituals play out in London, Gstaad, Dubai, New York, Paris, Bali and Kashmir — a star-tested itinerary any traveller can borrow.
articles.image_caption: The Manhattan skyline rises above the trees of Central Park in New York City. New York is one of seven destinations Bollywood stars return to year after year, beyond the usual Goa and Maldives getaways.
articles.nri_angle: Most of the stars' ritual destinations — London, New York, Dubai, Paris — are direct flights from US gateways, so diaspora travellers can lift this itinerary wholesale for their own next holiday.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
